subject: Proposed retention & locale-specific deletion language — redline review
messages:
From: Emma Collins <emma.collins@avocare.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@avocare.com, itops@avocare.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 17:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Questions on retention & deletion - redline of Annex B attached

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the call earlier. I've attached our redline of Annex B (AvoCare_AnnexB_Redline.pdf) and flagged a few items that we need clarified before legal can sign off:

1) Residency guarantee — our standard language requires customer content to be stored and processed only in the EU (no cross-border transfers) unless we provide 30 days' notice and obtain approval. Can Redwood commit to EU-only at-rest and processing for AvoCare production data?

2) Deletion timing — we asked for a contractual deletion confirmation within 30 days of termination or deletion request. Please confirm which systems/backups/replicas are covered and if you can provide a deletion certificate.

3) Backups & retention windows — we'd like clarity on: backups, cold archives, logs used for debugging, and billing records. Specifically, billing-related logs may need to be retained for up to 7 years for compliance; will Redwood accept that or propose a shorter limit?

4) Training & model use — confirm whether AvoCare content may be used to improve models. If not, please state that explicitly in the DPA. If yes, we require a time-limited retention window and opt-out mechanism.

5) Evidence — SOC2 reports and proof of deletion/audit logs are requested as part of our vendor review.

We pulled out what we think are the highest-impact asks; if you can provide proposed language and a couple of alternative windows (e.g., 30/45/90 days), that will help speed internal review.

Thanks,

Emma Collins
Senior Counsel, AvoCare Ltd
emma.collins@avocare.com

Attachment: AvoCare_AnnexB_Redline.pdf

From: jonas_weber@redwood.example <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
To: Emma Collins <emma.collins@avocare.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, neha_kapoor@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention & deletion - proposed Redwood language attached

Emma — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. I've looped in Laura (legal) and Neha (security) to help finalize text. Below is a concise proposal to address each point; attached is a word doc with full clause text (Redwood_Proposed_Retention_Clause_v1.docx).

Summary proposals (high level):
- Residency: Redwood will store and process AvoCare production content in the EU region for the duration of the agreement. Subprocessors operating outside the EU may be used only for non-content services (e.g., telemetry) and only after notice; customer content at rest will remain in EU storage.
- Deletion timing: Redwood will mark data for deletion within 24 hours of a validated request and complete logical deletion within 30 days. Physical deletion from backups/replicas will be completed within 90 days; Redwood will provide a signed deletion confirmation (certificate) within 45 days.
- Backups & billing logs: Billing and billing-related logs — propose 24 months retention as a compromise to your 7-year ask (we can provide limited extracts for audit on request).
- Training & model use: Redwood will not use customer content to train models without explicit, opt-in consent. If consented, Redwood will retain training snapshots for no longer than 180 days and will delete training artifacts thereafter.
- Evidence: Redwood will furnish the most recent SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and can provide deletion certificates and a redacted subprocessor list.

If any of the proposed windows are a hard stop for AvoCare, please flag them and we can escalate to execs for an exception.

Next steps: Laura will take these bullets and draft a tracked-changes version you can react to.

Best,

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.example
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Retention_Clause_v1.docx

Jonas / Laura / Neha,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We've reviewed your proposals and attached a second redline (AvoCare_AnnexB_Redline_v2.pdf) with our counterpoints. Main items:

- Residency: EU-only at-rest/processing for production is a must. We cannot accept broad subprocessors for processing customer content outside the EU even for telemetry — that needs to be expressly excluded.

- Deletion timing: 30 days for logical deletion is acceptable, but we need a guarantee that backups/replicas will be purged within 45 days (not 90), and we require the deletion certificate within 30 days of completion.

- Billing logs: we can be flexible, but 24 months is the minimum; given regulatory obligations we asked 7 years as a worst case. If Redwood can commit to 24 months with the ability to provide on-demand extracts going back to 7 years for legal reasons, that may work.

- Training: we require a contractual statement that customer content will not be used for model training unless AvoCare provides explicit written consent. The 180 day retention for training artifacts will need to be clearly limited and audited.

- Evidence: SOC2 plus an assurance that deletion certificates include a timestamped hash of deleted datasets (or equivalent audit identifier).

We're aiming to get final language by next week; can you confirm whether Laura can propose final tracked text that meets these constraints?

Best,

Emma Collins
Senior Counsel, AvoCare Ltd

Attachment: AvoCare_AnnexB_Redline_v2.pdf

From: laura_bennett@redwood.example <laura_bennett@redwood.example>

Subject: Re: Questions on retention & deletion - proposed final text attached

Emma — appreciate the clarity. We've reviewed your v2 redline and propose the following compromise text; full tracked changes are attached (Redwood_Final_Retention_Text_v2.docx). Key points: 

Proposed clause highlights (draft language snippet):
"Redwood shall store and process Customer Content for the provision of the Services in data centers located in the European Union. Customer Content at rest and in active processing shall remain within EU regions. Redwood may engage subprocessors outside the EU solely for non-customer-content services (e.g., monitoring infrastructure, analytics) provided Redwood gives Customer thirty (30) days' prior notice and an opportunity to object.

Upon Customer's deletion request or termination, Redwood will: (i) mark records for deletion within twenty-four (24) hours; (ii) complete logical deletion of active systems within thirty (30) days; and (iii) complete removal from backups and replicas within forty-five (45) days. Redwood will provide a signed deletion certificate within forty-five (45) days of completion, including an audit identifier and timestamp.

Billing and billing-related logs shall be retained for a period of twenty-four (24) months. Redwood will, upon Customer request and subject to reasonable security controls, provide extracts or attestations for historical billing data beyond twenty-four (24) months for legal or regulatory purposes.

Redwood will not use Customer Content to train models without Customer's explicit prior written consent. For any Customer Content used for training, Redwood will retain training artifacts for no longer than one hundred and eighty (180) days and will delete those artifacts thereafter; Redwood shall provide limited audit evidence of such deletion on request.
"

Operational notes:
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II under NDA and a redacted subprocessor list.
- The deletion certificate will include an audit identifier (hash or internal id) and timestamp; we will not disclose raw hashes of customer content but can provide identifiers that correlate with the deletion event.

If this aligns with AvoCare's needs, we will produce a final tracked Annex B and circulate for signature (DocuSign link will be provided). If any of these items are non-negotiable, please call them out and we'll escalate.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.example

Attachment: Redwood_Final_Retention_Text_v2.docx
